let FO enter and take the iPad first, otherwise hurry, sit and let him take
CPDLC — remind FO to transfer to ground
don't forget the takeoff briefing
CC briefing — taxi min is 10 mins out of SG, not 5; layer 2 is about how you can help them: will they be done with service by then, let them know you will release them after
equipment check had 2 things unchecked (item 3); cross-check local time
forgot to release my pitch at 100 kts
almost forgot to call flaps 0 — focus on flap retraction first, don't get distracted; pull speed if you want
watch speed as it reaches the Mach via perf page, press the speed button back to opti-climb speed
release autobrakes early when vacating (W7)
remember to start APU before turning in
when the load sheet arrives -> put in figures and cross check; write the pax on my sheet; go through with FO; get latest weather then cross-check performance
when there is a MEL -> brief the MEL ops procedure later, finish prep first
when there is a delay -> PA for delays
when a defect (e.g. wheel) and unsure -> put it in the ELB and get the engineer to sign; it is their problem to clear, not yours
Flight Pulse — filter by time; for WSSS switch to the airport tab instead of route to get an overview of all flights in
fuel decision — check Flight Pulse for a ZFW drop even when tankering and limited by MLW; it is ok to go FP fuel with data

flow — 1 let FO go in and take stuff, or get seated first; 2 set up seat, cockpit lights, headset, paper, licence, flow prep checklist; 3 fuel page + recall; 4 check books; 5 briefing; 6 preliminary fuel if you have it, FO goes down then fill the fuel cockpit column
digital CVR — no need for speakers off
IRS align — check the NAV page to cross-check when you get GPS PRIMARY LOST (to confirm reference with Pehon)
post box-setup scan — CLB NAV BLUE 1FD2, QNH 1013, seeing 20 ft PFD / ISIS 10 ft, HDG on standby 203, landing elevation AUTO, status good, navs aligned
can start preparing fuel and weights reason; put in the pax load when you get the load sheet
pax boarding — 320: 30 mins, 321: 35 mins
"set 11.4 on the panel" to FO when the fuel you want is 11.3

legal fuel required before pushback — use fuel and weights in Aviator; additional fuel requires consulting dispatch. After push use the same technique via Aviator less the contingency; additional is your call. If you need it you have to turn back, so it depends on weather
VDGS left/right calibration starts at 20 m; nose over the 320 line at 18 m, so roll until 18 m then slow down; braking is walking speed, no need to anticipate
ATC cannot enforce speed control during a hold; when exiting the hold go back to your ATC speed
after start flow is dual cooling first; if SETO it is yellow elec pump first
rotate faster; set 50% and wait for thrust to reach before going flex; cleared for takeoff when lining up — cut the corners, don't make a tight turn
Pehon called altitude — don't fly the FDs, especially ALT* or rolling out on heading, because it lags
when reducing speed let the nose go down before reducing speed, get the descent started
into Singapore was good; can be more precise following time with 500 fpm
flare into Bali was the right time but not enough rotation, hence a one-check flare; do the two-stage flare to get a level segment
do landing perf, know your distance
Q slope — can still maintain 10 kts then go 40% with SETI and hold until slightly before the downslope
profile was tight into Bali

messed up my takeoff briefing — brief RTO actions or EFATO actions
brief TEM — taxi error since it is in the INTAM, re-read the INTAM; consider T9 when 02L; clear shift or brief the proper procedure; see the threat to it

remember to brief usage of Flight Pulse to score points — in short, practise the briefing

check doors before releasing brakes — cargo doors were already open before I released the brakes

when preflight at the gate -> brief CC first, then give AWNF; get it out of the way, APC is more important than the misc stuff
when deciding fuel -> consider what if the runway closes: do you have enough fuel, what would you do
when SETO -> frequency change or turning on; takeoff can start if no traffic and 5 mins required, otherwise slightly before Romeo if there is an aircraft ahead
when holding the seat belts on for weather -> feel free to tell CC to hold the service; no need to take the risk
when bumping -> think about what is causing it: shifting winds, look at SAT as well
TROP — the higher is more conservative
wind modelling — request the lower and highest FL and the FMS will interpolate; insert CLB winds if there is time, also history winds
weather deviation — 1-in-60 rule; use your heading to determine the offset: 10 degrees = 10 miles
avoiding a super cell — 8000 ft and 60 NM
TAS increases about 2-3 kts per 1000 ft of elevation; take Vapp + wind factor, GS/2 gives your V/S, that is the estimated ROD

EDTO — fuel leak, smoke, dual engine failure, fire = fixed speed strategy VMO/MMO; other cases, even medical, follow the standard strategy — no rush, more stable approach, no need to overstress the aircraft with a chance of overspeed

sequence — 1 aerobridge retract; 2 tow truck connect, NW STRG; 3 3-5 mins to remove chocks (8 chocks, 3 grounding cables); 4 before headset connect tell FO to call for clearance when he hears it; 5 headset connect
reduce to 250 kts is enough; wait till 25 NM to 3200
direct to the point before the FAF to have a proper turn
can configure gear down a bit later, otherwise you are dragging in
flow — 1 start APU; 2 320 identified; 3 lights off / brake fans on / pressure is good; 4 area is clear
CJB altitudes (works with terrain): 1400 ground, 2400 stable, 3400 F2, 3800 F1
requested high speed below 10: increase to 300, start seeing it at 28 CCB; wind speed back from 300 to 250 at around 8500 ft; blue arrow 5-8 NM before is good enough for profile
decompression profile: set altitude constraints ISVUR +14000 and BAC +11000
headwind landing in; good flare and touchdown
